title: Improving Energy Efficiency of Uplink RSMA via Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver
summary: This paper investigates an uplink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) network empowered by a Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (RAQR) to maximize energy efficiency (EE). To overcome the amplitude-only measurement limitation of the considered direct readout RAQR, we devise a phase alignment mechanism that linearizes the received signal while retaining full channel energy, thereby enabling tractable optimization. The resulting non-convex fractional EE problem is transformed via Dinkelbach's method. For IoT scenarios with symmetric rate requirements, we derive exact closed-form power allocation from the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, which yields a globally optimal bisection search with negligible computational latency. For asymmetric rate requirements, we develop a generalized block coordinate descent-based power allocation (BCD-PA) framework that eliminates reliance on expensive interior-point solvers. We further propose a low-complexity paired allocation (LC-Paired) that exploits user pairing and closed-form bandwidth solutions via the Lambert-W function. Simulation results confirm that the KKT-based scheme attains the highest EE, while the BCD-PA offers a flexible complexity-performance trade-off. The LC-Paired scheme drastically reduces computational cost with only moderate EE degradation.

AI.tldr: 研究由里德堡原子量子接收机(RAQR)赋能的 uplink RSMA 网络能量效率最大化问题；提出相位对齐机制、Dinkelbach 变换，并针对对称/非对称速率需求分别给出 KKT 闭式、BCD-PA 与 LC-Paired 三种功分方案。
AI.motivation: 直接读出型 RAQR 只能测幅度，无法直接获得相位信息，导致接收信号与优化问题难以建模；同时 RSMA 功分与能量效率优化本身是非凸分式问题，且 IoT 设备算力受限，需要低复杂度、无需昂贵内点求解器的方案。
AI.method: 构建 RAQR 赋能 uplink RSMA 的 EE 最大化模型；设计相位对齐机制将接收信号线性化并保留全部信道能量；用 Dinkelbach 法将非凸分式问题转为凸差型迭代；对称速率场景由 KKT 条件导出闭式功分并配合二分搜索；非对称场景提出 BCD-PA 框架；进一步提出基于用户配对与 Lambert-W 闭式带宽解的 LC-Paired 低复杂度方案。
AI.result: 仿真显示：KKT 方案 EE 最高且计算时延可忽略；BCD-PA 在复杂度与性能间提供灵活折中；LC-Paired 大幅降低计算开销，仅带来中等 EE 损失。
AI.conclusion: 相位对齐 + Dinkelbach 的组合使幅度受限的 RAQR-RSMA 系统可解；分场景的功分设计能在有限算力下逼近最优 EE，为量子接收机赋能的 IoT 上行网络提供了可落地的低复杂度资源分配框架。
